background_notes.fact: With normalized torus measure the exponentials e^{ikx} form a complete orthonormal system in L2. Thus ||f||_2^2=sum_k |fhat(k)|^2, Fourier truncations converge in L2, and truncations converge in each Fourier-defined H^s norm for f in H^s. For square-summable sequences u,v, sum |u_k v_k| <= ||u||_ell2 ||v||_ell2.

Specifies the compatible Fourier coefficient normalization.
Defines H^s by completion and the weighted Fourier norm.
Uses orthogonality, Parseval, Cauchy–Schwarz and polynomial density for the indicated L2 and H^s inputs.

background_notes.justification: Orthogonality follows by integrating e^{i(k-l)x}. Completeness follows from density of trigonometric polynomials: Fejer kernels are nonnegative normalized approximate identities, their convolution approximates continuous periodic functions uniformly, and continuous functions are dense in L2 on this compact interval. The Hilbert-space completion of the finite coefficient isometry then gives Parseval. Weighted square-summable tails tend to zero, giving H^s truncation convergence. Finite Cauchy–Schwarz followed by increasing finite index sets gives the stated sequence inequality.

background_notes.fact: For A,B in Fourier H^1, A and B have bounded continuous representatives, their weak derivatives are in L2, ||A||_{H^1}^2=||A||_2^2+||partial_x A||_2^2, and AB belongs to H^1 with derivative (partial_x A)B+A(partial_x B). Consequently ||AB||_{H^1}<=C||A||_{H^1}||B||_{H^1}. Polynomial bilinear estimates continuous in these norms extend to the corresponding completions.

A0,B0 are H^1; S001 derives the Fourier L-infinity bound and inverse-derivative H^1 bound before using products and density.

background_notes.justification: The sum of <k>^(-2) is finite, so Cauchy–Schwarz gives absolute and uniform convergence of the H^1 Fourier series and its L-infinity bound. The derivative Fourier coefficients ik Ahat(k) are square summable, giving the weak derivative and norm identity. Apply the ordinary product rule to Fourier truncations. Their uniform convergence and convergence of derivatives in L2 imply convergence of each product-rule term in L2; testing against smooth functions passes the identity to the limit. The resulting bilinear bound also makes polynomial approximations Cauchy and their limits independent of the approximation. In particular this applies to S_t Dinv f and S_t Dinv g using the preceding multiplier estimates.

background_notes.fact: For F,G in normalized torus L2, FG is in L1, |(FG)hat(k)|<=||F||_2||G||_2 for each integer k, and (FG)hat(k)=sum_a Fhat(a)Ghat(k-a), with the latter sum absolutely convergent. If |Hhat(k)|<=M for all k, a Fourier multiplier m with sum_k |m(k)|^2<infinity sends H to an L2 distribution of norm at most M(sum_k |m(k)|^2)^(1/2).

background_notes.justification: Integral Cauchy–Schwarz gives integrability and the coefficient bound because |e^{-ikx}|=1. Approximate each factor in L2 by Fourier polynomials; the products converge in L1 by the same inequality. Coefficient convolution passes to the limit, since sequence Cauchy–Schwarz bounds both the absolute convolution and its approximation errors. The multiplier claim follows by termwise squaring and Parseval, or equivalently by the defining Fourier Sobolev completion. This justifies the products as actual distributions throughout S002.

background_notes.justification: Group positive integers into dyadic blocks [2^j,2^{j+1}); each block contributes at most 2^{j(1-q)}, and the resulting geometric series converges for q>1. Negative indices contribute the same amount. For |k|>=1, <k> is comparable to |k|, so the indicated series reduce to exponents 2 and 9/7.

background_notes.fact: For jointly smooth periodic spatial functions depending smoothly on a compact time interval, Fourier coefficients and each fixed time derivative decay faster than every inverse power of |k|, uniformly in time. The Fourier sums and product convolution sums in S003, after its finitely many differentiations, therefore converge absolutely and uniformly and can be differentiated or integrated termwise. A continuous function that is smooth on the pieces of a finite time partition has distributional time derivative equal to its piecewise derivative, without point masses at the partition points.

S_t has the explicit unit-modulus Fourier phase with time derivatives of polynomial frequency growth.

background_notes.justification: Repeated spatial integration by parts bounds the Fourier coefficient of each fixed time derivative by |k|^(-m) times a spatial-derivative norm bounded on the compact time interval. Choose m larger than all polynomial factors from the phase and derivatives. Summable uniform majorants then justify termwise differentiation and integration; the scalar fundamental theorem of calculus gives the endpoint identity coefficient by coefficient. In the piecewise case integration by parts against a compactly supported time test function produces boundary jumps only; continuity makes every interior jump zero. Summing the ordinary integral identities cancels the same interior endpoint values.
